course: Algebra 2 - Functions, Logarithms, Trigonometry and Series
attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
description: A full-year Algebra 2 course: polynomial and rational functions, complex numbers, exponents, radicals and logarithms, transformations, trigonometry, conic sections, sequences and series, probability and matrices.

concepts.title: Polynomials and their degree
concepts.summary: A polynomial is a sum of power terms, and its degree governs its end behaviour and how many roots it can have.

concepts.title: Adding and subtracting polynomials
concepts.summary: Like terms combine by their power, so addition and subtraction act on coefficients of the same degree.

concepts.title: Multiplying polynomials
concepts.summary: Every term of one polynomial multiplies every term of the other, which is the distributive property applied repeatedly.

concepts.title: Special polynomial products
concepts.summary: Perfect-square and difference-of-squares patterns let products be written without full distribution.

concepts.title: Factoring common factors
concepts.summary: Removing the greatest common factor is the first step of every factorisation.

concepts.title: Factoring by grouping
concepts.summary: Grouping pairs of terms with a shared factor turns a four-term polynomial into a product.

concepts.title: Factoring quadratics
concepts.summary: A quadratic factors into two linear factors whose constants satisfy the sum and product conditions.

concepts.title: Factoring sum and difference of cubes
concepts.summary: Sum and difference of cubes factor into a binomial and a quadratic using standard patterns.

concepts.title: The factor theorem
concepts.summary: A polynomial has a factor x minus c exactly when its value at c is zero.

concepts.title: The remainder theorem
concepts.summary: The remainder on dividing by x minus c equals the polynomial's value at c.

concepts.title: Long division of polynomials
concepts.summary: Polynomial long division mirrors integer long division and produces a quotient and a remainder.

concepts.title: Synthetic division
concepts.summary: Synthetic division divides by a linear factor quickly using only coefficients.

concepts.title: Factoring higher-degree polynomials
concepts.summary: Combining the factor theorem, division and pattern recognition factors polynomials of any degree.

concepts.title: End behaviour of polynomials
concepts.summary: The leading term decides what the graph does as the input grows large in either direction.

concepts.title: Zeros and multiplicity
concepts.summary: A repeated root makes the graph touch or flatten at the axis instead of crossing it.

concepts.title: Graphing polynomial functions
concepts.summary: Zeros, multiplicity, end behaviour and the y-intercept together determine the sketch.

concepts.title: The intermediate value theorem
concepts.summary: A continuous polynomial takes every value between its endpoint values, which locates real roots.

concepts.title: Symmetry in polynomial graphs
concepts.summary: Even and odd symmetry come from the parity of the exponents.

concepts.title: The imaginary unit i
concepts.summary: The imaginary unit squares to minus one, which gives negative numbers square roots.

concepts.title: Complex numbers and their arithmetic
concepts.summary: Complex numbers add componentwise and multiply by distributing, treating i squared as minus one.

concepts.title: Complex conjugates
concepts.summary: Multiplying by the conjugate removes the imaginary part, which is how a quotient is simplified.

concepts.title: Quadratic equations with complex solutions
concepts.summary: A negative discriminant gives a conjugate pair of complex roots.

concepts.title: The fundamental theorem of algebra
concepts.summary: A degree-n polynomial has exactly n complex roots counted with multiplicity.

concepts.title: Rational exponents
concepts.summary: A fractional exponent is a root, so radicals and powers are two notations for the same thing.

concepts.title: Simplifying radical expressions
concepts.summary: Radicals simplify by removing perfect-power factors and rationalising denominators.

concepts.title: Radical equations
concepts.summary: Squaring both sides can introduce extraneous solutions, so every result must be checked.

concepts.title: Graphing square and cube root functions
concepts.summary: Root graphs have restricted domains and characteristic shapes that transform like other functions.

concepts.title: Exponential growth and decay
concepts.summary: A quantity changes by a constant factor per period, which is multiplicative rather than additive.

concepts.title: Graphing exponential functions
concepts.summary: Exponential graphs have a horizontal asymptote and pass through the point zero one.

concepts.title: The number e and continuous growth
concepts.summary: Continuous compounding leads to the base e, which describes growth as a rate.

concepts.title: Compound interest
concepts.summary: Compound interest applies the growth factor repeatedly, and more frequent compounding raises the effective rate.
prerequisites: The number e and continuous growth

concepts.title: Introduction to logarithms
concepts.summary: A logarithm answers the exponent question, and it is the inverse of the exponential.

concepts.title: Properties of logarithms
concepts.summary: Products, quotients and powers become sums, differences and multiples of logs.

concepts.title: Solving exponential equations with logarithms
concepts.summary: Taking a logarithm of both sides isolates an unknown exponent.

concepts.title: Solving logarithmic equations
concepts.summary: Rewriting in exponential form solves log equations, and every solution must be checked for domain.

concepts.title: Graphing logarithmic functions
concepts.summary: A log graph is the reflection of its exponential in the line y equals x.

concepts.title: Change of base
concepts.summary: Change of base rewrites a logarithm in any base, which makes any log computable.

concepts.title: Function transformations
concepts.summary: Shifts, stretches and reflections move a parent graph without changing its shape family.

concepts.title: Shifting and reflecting graphs
concepts.summary: Horizontal changes act inside the function and reverse intuition, while vertical changes act outside.

concepts.title: Stretching and compressing graphs
concepts.summary: A factor greater than one stretches and a factor between zero and one compresses.

concepts.title: Even and odd functions
concepts.summary: Even functions are symmetric about the y-axis and odd functions about the origin.

concepts.title: Inverse functions
concepts.summary: An inverse undoes a function, and it exists only where the function is one-to-one.

concepts.title: Composite functions
concepts.summary: A composite applies one function to the output of another, and order matters.

concepts.title: Rational expressions and simplification
concepts.summary: A rational expression is a quotient of polynomials, simplified by cancelling common factors.

concepts.title: Multiplying and dividing rational expressions
concepts.summary: Multiplication and division work like fractions, with factoring first.

concepts.title: Adding and subtracting rational expressions
concepts.summary: A common denominator is required, exactly as with numerical fractions.

concepts.title: Solving rational equations
concepts.summary: Multiplying by the common denominator can introduce extraneous solutions, so results must be checked.

concepts.title: Asymptotes and holes
concepts.summary: Vertical asymptotes come from non-cancelled factors and holes from cancelled ones.

concepts.title: Graphing rational functions
concepts.summary: Intercepts, asymptotes and holes together determine the shape of a rational graph.

concepts.title: Solving exponential and logarithmic equations
concepts.summary: Choosing the right inverse isolates the unknown in either direction.

concepts.title: Solving systems with nonlinear equations
concepts.summary: Substitution reduces a nonlinear system to one equation in one variable.

concepts.title: Absolute value equations and inequalities
concepts.summary: Absolute value splits into two cases, and inequalities require checking the direction.

concepts.title: Linear and quadratic models
concepts.summary: Constant difference suggests a linear model and constant second difference a quadratic one.

concepts.title: Exponential and logarithmic models
concepts.summary: A constant ratio suggests exponential growth or decay.

concepts.title: Choosing a model and checking fit
concepts.summary: Residuals and context decide which model is defensible.

concepts.title: Angles and radian measure
concepts.summary: Radians measure an angle by arc length, which makes calculus and periodicity natural.

concepts.title: The unit circle
concepts.summary: The unit circle gives sine and cosine as coordinates and extends them beyond right triangles.

concepts.title: Sine, cosine and tangent
concepts.summary: The three basic ratios relate the sides of a right triangle and extend to any angle.

concepts.title: Graphing trigonometric functions
concepts.summary: Amplitude, period, phase and midline describe a transformed sinusoid.

concepts.title: Trigonometric identities
concepts.summary: Pythagorean, sum and double-angle identities rewrite expressions and prove equalities.

concepts.title: Solving trigonometric equations
concepts.summary: Periodicity means a trigonometric equation usually has infinitely many solutions.

concepts.title: Inverse trigonometric functions
concepts.summary: Inverse functions recover an angle, restricted to a principal range to stay one-to-one.

concepts.title: Parabolas
concepts.summary: A parabola is the set of points equidistant from a focus and a directrix.

concepts.title: Circles
concepts.summary: A circle is the set of points a fixed distance from a centre.

concepts.title: Ellipses
concepts.summary: An ellipse is the set of points whose distances to two foci sum to a constant.

concepts.title: Hyperbolas
concepts.summary: A hyperbola is the set of points whose distances to two foci differ by a constant.

concepts.title: Identifying conic sections
concepts.summary: The general second-degree equation is classified by its coefficients.

concepts.title: Arithmetic sequences and series
concepts.summary: An arithmetic sequence adds a constant difference and its series sum has a closed form.

concepts.title: Geometric sequences and series
concepts.summary: A geometric sequence multiplies by a constant ratio, and its finite sum also has a closed form.

concepts.title: Summation notation
concepts.summary: Sigma notation compresses a sum and makes index changes explicit.

concepts.title: Infinite geometric series
concepts.summary: An infinite geometric series converges exactly when the common ratio is smaller than one in size.

concepts.title: The binomial theorem
concepts.summary: Binomial coefficients from Pascal's triangle expand a power of a binomial.

concepts.title: The counting principle
concepts.summary: Independent choices multiply, which is the basis of all counting.

concepts.title: Permutations and combinations
concepts.summary: Permutations count ordered arrangements and combinations count unordered selections.

concepts.title: Probability with combinatorics
concepts.summary: Counting favourable and total outcomes gives a probability for equally likely events.

concepts.title: Matrix notation and operations
concepts.summary: Matrices are rectangular arrays, and addition and scalar multiplication act entrywise.

concepts.title: Matrix multiplication
concepts.summary: Matrix multiplication combines rows of the first with columns of the second, so order matters.

concepts.title: Determinants
concepts.summary: A determinant is a number that reports whether a matrix is invertible.

concepts.title: Inverse matrices
concepts.summary: An inverse matrix undoes a linear transformation, and it exists only when the determinant is non-zero.

concepts.title: Solving systems with matrices
concepts.summary: A linear system can be solved by matrix inverse or row reduction.
